aisha_named: false (Khadija named as Χαδίγαν; Aisha not mentioned)
ref: Theophanes, Chronographia, ed. C. de Boor, vol. 1 (Leipzig 1883), p. 334, under AM 6122 (AD 629/630)
url: https://archive.org/download/bub_gb_QlPPAAAAMAAJ/bub_gb_QlPPAAAAMAAJ_djvu.txt (p. 334 region of the de Boor text; OCR read)
quote_orig: κατ᾽ ὀλίγον δὲ παρρησιασάμενος ὑπεισῆλθε τῇ γυναικὶ χήρᾳ οὔσῃ, καὶ ἔλαβεν αὐτὴν γυναῖκα καὶ ἔσχε τὰς καμήλους αὐτῆς καὶ τὴν ὕπαρξιν. ἐρχόμενος δὲ ἐν Παλαιστίνῃ συνανεστρέφετο Ἰουδαίοις τε καὶ Χριστιανοῖς.
own_translation_en: Little by little, after making himself bold, he went in to the woman, a widow, and took her as his wife, and got her camels and her property. Travelling in Palestine he kept company with Jews and Christians.
quote_latin: paulatim vero liberiore eius utens consuetudine, ut erat vidua, se in gratiam eius insinuavit, adeo ut uxorem ipsam duxerit, eiusque camelos universamque substantiam fecerit suam. (Bonn 1839 Latin printed beside the Greek; translator not identified on the page read.)
licence_note: Public domain (Teubner 1883). The Greek is OCR from the Google scan on archive.org; the Bonn 1839 Greek shows the same phrase ('καὶ ἔλαβεν αὐτὴν γυναῖκα') so it is cross-checked. No public-domain English translation found; not quoted.
what_it_says: Theophanes narrates that Muhammad, a poor orphan, took as wife the rich widow Khadija and got her property. He gives no age for either.
context: Part of the AM 6122 entry, where Theophanes reports Muhammad's death and successor and then gives a biographical excursus on his origin and rise. The marriage described is to Khadija; there is no mention of Aisha.
limits: Not about Aisha or her age; the marriage is presented neutrally; Greek OCR; the passage is the author's own narrative, not an opponent's criticism.

aisha_named: false (Abu Bakr named as Ἀβουβάχαρος, Muhammad's relative and successor; his daughter Aisha is not mentioned)
ref: Theophanes, Chronographia, ed. C. de Boor (1883), p. 333, under AM 6122; Bonn 1839 p. 512 region (Latin: 'Abubachar cognato suo successore designato')
quote_orig: Τούτῳ τῷ ἔτει ἀπεβίω Μουάμεδ, ὁ τῶν Σαρακηνῶν ἀρχηγὺς καὶ ψευδοπροφήτης, προχειρισάμενος ᾽άβουβάχαρον συγγενῆ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὴν ἀρχὴν αὐτοῦ.
own_translation_en: In this year Muamed, leader of the Saracens and false prophet, died, having appointed Abubacharos, his relative, to his office.
quote_latin: Hoc anno Muamed Saracenorum dux et pseudopropheta, Abubachar cognato suo successore designato, mortuus est. (Bonn 1839; the word 'Abuba-' is hyphenated at the line break in the scan and is joined here.)
licence_note: Public domain. Greek OCR (de Boor) cross-checked with the Latin of the 1839 Bonn edition.
what_it_says: Theophanes says Muhammad, at his death, appointed Abubacharos, his relative, as successor.
context: Same entry as theo-6122-khadija. Theophanes uses Abu Bakr only as successor; he does not connect him to a daughter or a marriage.
limits: Establishes only the name of Aisha's father in a Greek source, not her name or any marriage. Greek variants in the de Boor apparatus include Βουβέκερ and Ἀβουμάχαρ.

aisha_named: false (Aisha not named in this title)
ref: Euthymius Zigabenus, Panoplia dogmatica, Titulus XXVIII 'Adversus Saracenos', §18 (as numbered in the text), PG 130, between printed pages 1349 and 1353 (exact column not determined from OCR)
own_translation_en: He laid down the law that each of you may take four wives; and concubines, a thousand, or as many as one can keep.
quote_latin: Hic legem tulit, ut quisque vestrum quatuor uxores ducere queat; pellices vero mille, aut quotquot aliquis alere possit. (OCR reads 'Hie', 'qustuor' and a split 'quot-quot'; corrected here.)
licence_note: Latin is the 1595 Sylburg text printed beside the Greek (PG footnote). Greek of this sentence is illegible in the OCR, so quote_orig is empty. Public domain.
what_it_says: Zigabenus says Muhammad's law allowed each believer four wives and as many concubines as he could maintain.
context: Part of the Saracen title, in the section after Zigabenus has described Muhammad's marriage to a rich widow (Khadija) and his later conduct. The number of wives is the target; no named wife appears in this sentence.
limits: Criticism concerns the number of wives and concubines, not Aisha or an age. Compilatory text (PG note: largely drawn from earlier patristic writers, not from first-hand knowledge). OCR-only Latin check; Greek not quoted.

aisha_named: true: Greek 'ἀϊσέ' as OCR 'και την ’ΑϊσΕ' (Greek of PG 104 col. not determined; OCR reads 'ΑϊσΕ', the final letter may be lowercase έ); Latin 'Aise'
ref: Bartholomaeus Edessenus, Elenchus et confutatio Agareni, PG 104 (Migne, Series graeca tomus CIV), section on Muhammad's wives and children; column not determined from the OCR
own_translation_en: He had four first and principal wives: Zadize, Aise, Zeinep and Omielteim. He had a daughter, Phatma, whom he gave in marriage to Ali; and two sons, Hasan and Husayn.
quote_latin: Uxores vero primas et numero quatuor habuit: videlicet Zadize, Aise, Zeinep, et Omielteim. Habuit vero filiam nomine Phatmam, quam genero Alim matrimonio locavit. Habuit et duos filios Chousanen et Chousainen.
licence_note: Le Moyne 1685 Greek-Latin text as reproduced in PG 104 (public domain). The Greek name is OCR-only and must be checked against the page image before use; the Latin is clean in the OCR.
what_it_says: Bartholomew names Aise as one of Muhammad's four principal wives, in a list with Zadize, Zeinep and Omielteim. He gives no age and no criticism of her marriage in this sentence.
context: Follows the account of Muhammad's marriage to Khadija and of the Zayd episode; the author presents Muhammad's family as part of a refutation.
limits: Earliest Greek text found that names Aisha, but the date of Bartholomew is uncertain (PG notitia: 'aetatis admodum incerta'); the PG editor says the list of wives and children disagrees in names and numbers with the anonymous text printed with it; Greek name from OCR only.

ref: Bartholomaeus Edessenus, Elenchus, PG 104 (section on the Zayd episode, before the wives list); column not determined
own_translation_en: He had a friend called Zez, who had a very beautiful wife married to him. Muhammad, fired with love for her, wanted to have her for himself.
quote_latin: Habebat quippe amicum nomine Zez, cui matrimonio juncta erat uxor formae elegantissimae. Illius vero amore accensus Muhammed, voluit illam sibi vim habere et obtinere.
licence_note: Latin printed beside the Greek in PG 104 (Le Moyne 1685). Greek OCR too interleaved to quote; quote_orig empty.
what_it_says: Bartholomew says Muhammad desired the wife of his friend Zayd and tried to take her.
context: The Zayd episode precedes the list of Muhammad's wives in the Elenchus; the author treats it as a sign of lust, not as a story about Aisha.
limits: No Aisha, no age; the charge is of lust toward another man's wife (LUST by content; the naming condition of the team's LUST definition is not met). Date of the text uncertain.

ref: Bartholomaeus Edessenus, Elenchus, PG 104, section on the law of four wives (after the Zayd episode); column not determined
own_translation_en: (The author states that any Hagarene may, in plain words, take four wives in marriage, live with them openly, and take as many concubines as he likes.)
quote_latin: illa disertis verbis quemlibet Hagarenorum posse sibi quatuor uxores matrimonio copulare, et cum illis publice consuescere, concubinas vero tot quot illi placuerit.
licence_note: Latin printed beside the Greek (PG 104). Greek OCR not usable here.
keys: concubinas vero tot quot illi placuerit
what_it_says: Bartholomew states that Muhammad's law allows each of the Agarenes four wives and as many concubines as he wishes.
context: Same section as bart-zayd-lust; here the author draws the general consequence of the law of wives.
limits: No Aisha, no age; criticism concerns the law of marriage and concubines, not a named wife (naming condition not met).

ref: Nicetas Choniates, Thesaurus orthodoxae fidei, book XX (on the Agarenes), §6, PG 140 (printed page marker 111 of the Choniates section per OCR)
own_translation_en: Hence he laid down openly that four wives may be taken, and concubines, if one can, even a thousand or as many as one may acquire, subject to the four wives.
quote_latin: Porro in hoc quod diximus de muliere capitulo, quatuor uxores palam duci lege statuit, et concubinas si quis poterit etiam mille vel quotquot cujusque manus adquisiverit, quatuor uxoribus subditas : ex quibus siquam dimittere voluerit, atque aliam ducere, hanc ob causam legem tulit.
licence_note: Latin printed beside the Greek in PG 140 (Mai's text, per the page header). Greek lines are interleaved in the OCR; a partial Greek (OCR) reads 'τέσσαρας γυ-ναῖκα[ς] ... ταῖς τέσσαρσι γυναιξίν' but is not quoted. Public domain.
keys: quatuor uxores palam duci lege statuit
concubinas si quis poterit etiam mille
what_it_says: Choniates says Muhammad's law permits four wives openly, plus concubines without limit as far as a man can support them, all subject to the four wives, and allows repudiation and remarriage.
context: Book XX of the Thesaurus, section on the 'chapter on women' of the Qur'an as the author reads it; the author then recounts the Zayd episode.
limits: Criticism of law and number of wives; no Aisha; no age. Polemical source, writing c. 1200 (approximate). Latin is the facing translation, its translator not identified on the page read.

ref: Nicetas Choniates, Thesaurus orthodoxae fidei, book XX, §6 (the Zayd episode), PG 140
own_translation_en: Then, after taking her, Muhammad committed adultery and afterwards made the law: that whoever wishes may send away his wife.
quote_latin: Tunc illa ducta Mohamedes, et moechatus, hanc postea legem tulit: nempe ut quisquis voluerit, uxorem suam dimittat.
licence_note: Latin facing the Greek (PG 140). Public domain. Sentence is short (17 words), kept because it is the author's explicit charge of adultery.
what_it_says: Choniates charges that Muhammad took Zayd's wife and committed adultery, and that he afterwards made a law permitting repudiation.
context: Continues the account of the four-wives law; the Zayd episode is given as its origin.
limits: No Aisha, no age; the adultery charge concerns the wife of Zayd, not Aisha. Polemic; the OCR wording is joined across a page break in the Latin text.
